title.suggested: Dispatch Correspondent's Account of the Allen-Goss Fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch's correspondent described the Allen-Goss fight near Walton, Kentucky: Allen drew first blood before the Covington militia arrived, and the headlines said Goss was given the fight on a foul.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Dispatch, Thursday Evening, September 7, 1876 (First Edition, 3 P.M.). Predates the 1878 Post-Dispatch merger.

facts.fact: Allen fought Joe Goss at a spot three miles below Walton Station, Kentucky, about eighteen miles below Cincinnati, with Eph Holland as referee
Allen drew first blood in the first round; the Covington Light Guards and another militia company arrived after the third round
The headlines report that after a second ring was pitched Allen battered Goss, but Goss was given the fight on a foul and Allen was put in the Newport jail

notes: Recrop to include the continuation in the second column. The third fact comes from the headlines only, since the body text describing it is outside the clipping.
